- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next period.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >+10% for 3–5 days), consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating 0.33/0.67), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment).
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; apply lagged sentiment filter: if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), check for sentiment-driven overconfidence — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
